links.outcome: Vendor selection through side-by-side simulation and workflow demonstrations of 4 ambient scribe vendors
links.effect: Multiphase comparison of 4 vendors, narrowed to 2 and then 1, reported to have minimized vendor influence and cognitive bias in selection; no comparative counterfactual outcome reported.
links.quote: Our structured, multiphase evaluation process minimized vendor influence and cognitive bias during selection, validated results through real-world clinical testing, and enabled a system-wide rollout.

links.outcome: Local pilot assessment of documentation time and patient satisfaction after ambient scribe deployment
links.effect: 35.4% decrease in pajama time (P=.054) and 28.3% decrease in time in notes (n=23; P<.001); patient satisfaction improved across domains (all P<.001).
links.quote: The pilot showed a 35.4% decrease in pajama time (P=.054, trend toward significance) and a 28.3% decrease in time in notes (n=23; P<.001).

links.outcome: Coding level shifts and visit volume after ambient scribe pilot
links.effect: 3.8% increase in level 4 established patient visits (P=.05); established patient volumes up 8.5%; projected revenue gain of US $2629 per provider per month.
links.quote: Coding patterns shifted toward higher-complexity visits, with a 3.8% increase in level 4 established patient visits (P=.05), and established patient volumes increased by 8.5%, which was associated with a projected revenue gain of US $2629 per provider per month.

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating a structured, multiphase simulation and live-pilot evaluation framework for selecting and safely deploying ambient clinical documentation AI in a health system.

primary.practice: multiphase evaluation and vendor selection framework
